label: Glass
//: A theme restates tokens and nothing else - see the Themes section of docs/RULES.md. The first cut of this file restated ten tokens and stopped at the surface colours, on a reading that the hard block and the square corner were the language rather than the theme. That reading was too narrow and it showed: translucent panels wearing an opaque theme's block did not read as glass, they read as a bug. What is actually fixed is the one-for-one rule - no invented token, no second selector, no component that exists only here - and this file now restates the block and the corner alongside the surface layer, because those are how a theme says what its material is. What it still leaves alone: the five saturated fills, the measure and the type. The offset scale the block is composed from is restated too - see //offset, which is where that reading was narrowed a second time.
//surfaces: The two surfaces become cool gradients at real alpha rather than white at .09. The gradient is rule 1's one relief and the alpha is rule 2's, and both are confined to the surface layer where those rules put them. The 145deg fall from a lighter top-left to a darker bottom-right is what makes a pane read as tilted toward a light rather than as a translucent rectangle. --axi-ink-line and --axi-rule follow them to a cool near-white at low alpha: the edge of a pane of glass is as much the pane as its face, and an opaque hairline around it is a picture frame.
//float: A floating panel keeps the 145deg tilt and loses the transparency. This is the token the language added for exactly this theme: a pane at .42 alpha is legible sitting on the page and illegible the moment a table scrolls under it, and the blur cannot be relied on to save it because backdrop-filter is missing or disabled on whole platforms. .97 rather than 1 so the edge still catches the page light and the pane still reads as glass rather than as a grey box that wandered in from another theme.
//ground: The page drops to #0a0c10 and takes its light from --axi-ground-image, three wide radials - violet top-left, cyan upper-right, rose bottom - which is the second token this theme cost the language and the reason it exists. The light lives on body alone. --axi-ground stays a flat colour because the plot and the select read it as background-color, where an image is invalid, and because a page-positioned radial inside a 30px chip would be an arbitrary wedge of colour. --axi-ground-deep drops to rgba(12, 14, 18, .72) rather than following the relit line. The three shapes MADE of that ink - the tooltip, the titlebar strip, the switch's slug - keep their dark, but stop being opaque: an opaque near-black strip across the top of a translucent window is the single loudest thing that stops this theme reading as glass, because the chrome is the one part of the app a reader never scrolls away. .72 rather than lower because the tooltip is the strictest consumer - it sits over arbitrary content and must stay legible when backdrop-filter is missing or switched off, the same constraint that bought --axi-surface-float. The blur comes from --axi-surface-filter, which .axi-titlebar and .axi-tooltip both apply and which is none on every other surface, so this costs those surfaces nothing.
//well: --axi-well-fill defaults to --axi-ground, which is right wherever surfaces are opaque - a hole in a panel shows the page. Here it would be an opaque near-black patch inside a translucent pane, which reads as a bug rather than a recess, so it is restated as a darkening at alpha and the pane's own tint carries through it. --axi-well-line needs no restating: it follows --axi-rule, which this theme has already lifted to the cool near-white the panel edges use.
//inks: --axi-accent-ink and --axi-ink-on-fill default to var(--axi-ink-line), so relighting the line would drag them with it and write pale text on saturated fills. They are restated at the old dark for that reason alone: the ink a filled button writes in has not changed, it has only stopped being spelled as the outline.
//block: The block becomes a soft drop plus an inset top highlight, and the borders drop to 1px. Rule 3 asks that a raised element read as raised and an outlined one as outlined; a hard 6px offset in near-black is the main theme's answer and this is glass's. The inset white line along the top edge is the whole trick - it is a specular highlight, the thing that separates a pane of glass from a grey rectangle - and it is spelled as part of the composed shadow because that is the one place the language lets a theme restate what raising a thing looks like. The corners round to 16/10px for the same reason: a square corner on a translucent pane reads as a cut, not an edge.
//offset: The offset scale zeroes out. The main theme composes its block from --axi-offset-panel/-control and their hover pair, and --axi-shadow-* is where a theme restates what raising a thing looks like - which this file does. The offsets underneath were left standing on a reading that they were the language rather than the theme, and that reading shipped a bug: consumers that compose a block from the offsets directly, instead of asking for --axi-shadow-panel, kept the main theme's hard 6px near-black plate under a theme that had already said its relief is a soft drop. The plate read as a stray backdrop behind every card, and on a rounded corner it read as broken rounding. Zeroing them is the one-for-one rule applied honestly: the offset scale IS part of what a theme's material is, so a theme that restates the block restates the scale it was composed from. A consumer still on the offsets now gets no relief rather than the wrong one; the fix on that side is to ask for the composed block.

tokens.--axi-ground-image: radial-gradient(900px 500px at 15% 0%, rgba(120, 90, 255, .30), transparent 60%), radial-gradient(700px 500px at 95% 30%, rgba(0, 190, 255, .22), transparent 62%), radial-gradient(600px 600px at 60% 100%, rgba(255, 90, 170, .20), transparent 60%)

//paint: Each of the surfaces this theme paints with a gradient also restates its -paint companion, the same surface as one flat <color>, because a token holding a gradient can only ever BE a background and consumers want these fills in places that take a colour - a chart's fill, an operand of color-mix(), a border-color. See --axi-surface-paint in tokens.css for why that is a companion rather than a split. The values are not a fresh judgement: each is the midpoint of the gradient above it, the colour that gradient is a narrow spread around. Restating them is not optional for a theme that grades a surface - the companions are aliased to the surfaces in tokens.css, so a theme that grades one and forgets the other hands the gradient straight back. Glass is where the independent check is sharpest: rgba(43, 50, 69, .485) and rgba(65, 76, 100, .44) land within three per channel, and at an identical alpha, of the --bg-card and --bg-hover axibridge had pinned by eye in its own stylesheet to work around not having them.
